picks.style: archaic greek chorus, aulos and low drone, elders' voices in unison, foreboding, measured
picks.why: "What mortal man can escape the guile of god?" — Delusion's fair face, the emptied city, the army gone off like bees in a swarm.

picks.style: greek threnody, bowed lyre and frame drum, mixed voices, slow, desolate then defiant
picks.why: The empire ending in one image: the blood-stained soil of Salamis holds all that once was Persia, and tongues go free.

picks.style: necromantic invocation, deep drone, struck bronze, chanting male voices, ritual, hypnotic
picks.why: The summoning of Darius from the tomb — libations poured, Earth and Hermes called, a chant with its own liturgy.

picks.style: roman chorus, plucked lyre and low strings, calm unison voices, plain, steady, consoling
picks.why: Beechwood cups held without a trembling hand against blood mingled with golden ones — the whole moral fits in the images.

picks.style: orphic hymn, solo lyre and soft drone, warm baritone, spellbound, slow
picks.why: Orpheus in the underworld: the wheel stilled, Tityos' liver healed, Tantalus forgetting his thirst while the song lasts.

picks.style: apotheosis hymn, harp and strings with rising choir, radiant, broad, exalted
picks.why: Spring, summer, autumn, winter turning past a fixed star — "sooner shall the harvest be born in the deep" than his praises fall silent.

picks.style: philosophical hymn, chamber organ and strings, noble tenor, broad, reverent
picks.why: The Hymn of Cleanthes in couplets — one god under many names, and every living thing an embodied portion of the soul divine.

picks.style: baroque masque chorus, recorders, harpsichord and light strings, treble voices, airy, quick
picks.why: "From the moon's relucent horn, from the star that wakes the morn" — spirits summoned in trochaics, with a chorus already written in.

picks.style: spenserian pastoral, lute and viol, gentle baritone, flowing, archaic
picks.why: Two clean Spenserian stanzas on a long marriage and the grove of children around the sacred olive.

picks.style: english elegy, solo cello and chamber organ, low unhurried baritone, hushed, twilit
picks.why: The curfew, the lowing herd, the ploughman — the most famous opening in English elegy, and it needs nothing around it.

picks.style: welsh bardic lament, harp alone then storm of strings, wild declaiming male voice, building, tempestuous
picks.why: The Bard on the rock above Conway, beard streaming like a meteor, striking the deep sorrows of his lyre.

picks.style: nordic war chant, bowed lyre and heavy drums, layered female voices with a repeating refrain, driving, grim
picks.why: The Fatal Sisters weaving: "Pikes must shiver, javelins sing" and the bracketed refrain "Weave the crimson web of war".

picks.style: georgian comic air, harpsichord and flute, arch light tenor, trotting, teasing
picks.why: Cupid stepping out of the rose bush: if so small a dart in the finger smarts, what if I had pierced your heart?

picks.style: 18th century dramatic air, strings and continuo, biting baritone, urgent, imperious
picks.why: The poet revoking the beauty he claims to have lent — pagan priests dressing the wood, then falling before the senseless god.

picks.style: roman drinking epigram set to music, lyre and hand drum, playful tenor, loose, late-night swing
picks.why: Martial sending his Muse only after dark — when Lyaeus rages, the rose reigns and the hair is dripping — then even rigid Catos may read.

picks.style: greek heroic lyric, solo lyre with sea-drone, clear resonant male voice, echoing, slow, luminous
picks.why: Achilles' own song to Echo across the Black Sea, asking her to sing Homer back to him — a complete lyric with a real conceit.

picks.style: music hall ballad, upright piano and banjo, wry working-class voice, jaunty, deadpan
picks.why: Only candidate, and it is a complete four-line epitaph — the heavens ringing with psalms while she does nothing for ever and ever.
